title: Seal the tomb (Matthew 27:57–66)
hook: a kindness nobody can pay back, and a stone the powerful make as sure as they can
carry: make it as sure as you can
tomorrow: the stone is sealed and guarded. so who's sitting on it?

segments.voice: Darkness, a torn veil, a soldier's words at the cross: truly this was the son of god. Then evening comes, and there is a body to bury.
screen: `TRULY THIS WAS THE SON OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Some favors can be paid back: a ride, a loan, a borrowed charger. Some never can. When the even was come, a rich man of Arimathaea named Joseph, also a disciple, goes to Pilate and asks for the body of Jesus. He wraps it in clean linen and lays it in his own new tomb, cut out of the rock. He rolls a great stone to the door, and goes. Two women stay: "And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre."
screen: `SOME FAVORS CAN'T BE PAID BACK.` → `HIS OWN NEW TOMB.` → `TWO WOMEN STAY.`

segments.voice: Here's the question underneath: what do you owe someone who can never pay you back? Matthew's answer is Joseph: his own tomb, clean linen, a great stone, and no thanks possible. Now a neighbor, and this one is close to home. Joseph is doing what his own scripture asked. The Torah says a body hanged on a tree must not stay there through the night; bury it the same day. And Jewish tradition has a name for this work. When Jacob asks his son to deal kindly and truly with him and bury him, the teacher Rashi explains that kindness to the dead is chesed shel emet, true kindness, because the one you help can never repay you. So Christians and Jews share this: burying the dead is love with no return address. The honest difference: Matthew tells this burial as a pause before the third day, and Christians read it toward Easter; Judaism does not share that belief about Jesus. Then the next day. The chief priests and Pharisees remember Jesus said, "After three days I will rise again," and ask for the tomb to be secured. Pilate: "Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can." "So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch." They already have what they wanted, and still can't rest without a stone, a seal and soldiers.
screen: `WHAT DO YOU OWE THE DEAD?` · `CHESED SHEL EMET: TRUE KINDNESS.` · `AFTER THREE DAYS I WILL RISE.` · `SEALING THE STONE, SETTING A WATCH.` · then, large: `MAKE IT AS SURE AS YOU CAN.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people who did something for you that you can never pay back: someone who has died, a teacher long gone, a stranger who helped and left. Let each finger fold down slowly with a name or a face. If you run out of fingers, start again.
Seal the tomb. A great stone, a seal on it, and soldiers set to make it as sure as anyone could.
Your line: make it as sure as you can, Pilate's words over a sealed stone. Rest well tonight.

screen: `DAY 1483 COUNTS.` → `MATTHEW, READ THROUGH · 57 OF 60.` → `TOMORROW: THE STONE IS SEALED AND GUARDED. SO WHO'S SITTING ON IT?`

howItsDone: Some churches keep Holy Saturday, the day between Good Friday and Easter, as a quiet day of waiting at the tomb; in Jewish communities, caring for and burying the dead is honored as a kindness that cannot be repaid.

notes: UNITY THREAD (wisdom day): shared ground with Judaism, in its own sources: Deuteronomy 21:22–23 (burial the same day; paraphrased) and Rashi on Genesis 47:29, who explains 'kindly and truly' as chesed shel emet, true kindness, since the dead cannot repay (paraphrased). A Jewish Keeper should confirm the paraphrases, the transliteration and that 'love with no return address' is a fair summary.

Honest difference as voiced: 'Matthew tells this burial as a pause before the third day, and Christians read it toward Easter; Judaism does not share that belief about Jesus.' Confirm it says who believes what without ranking.

'Joseph is doing what his own scripture asked' links Joseph's evening burial to Deuteronomy 21:22–23; Matthew 27:57 says only 'when the even was come'. A scholar should confirm the link is fair to state this way (other Gospels make the timing explicit).

The chief priests and Pharisees are named as Matthew names them (27:62) and are not made the foil; the trap of the scene is 'the powerful', Pilate included. Their phrase 'that deceiver' (27:63) is left out. Confirm.
The carry 'make it as sure as you can' modernizes the KJV 'make it as sure as ye can' (27:65); the voice quotes the KJV.

Practice: the outline's practice ('notice what the powerful try to seal') is carried by the fork; the sit itself is a gratitude count for kindness that can't be repaid, tied to the wisdom thread. Confirm.

Grace storyline, day 13: Grace is at the burial of Nia's grandma June; Nia (family not religious) whispers 'what's the point, she can't even know we came'. The skimmer's option pushes a belief onto Nia's family; the right reply offers the shared idea of kindness that can't be repaid.
